lead: For most visitors the best theme park in Dubai is IMG Worlds of Adventure at €63: 22 rides fully indoors and air-conditioned, so the heat never decides your day, and children under 105 cm get in free. Want two parks in one day? The Dubai Parks Multi Parks Pass (€88) adds a second park for about €15.

On IMG Worlds vs Motiongate: IMG wins on price and comfort, Motiongate (€73) on coasters, with 5 of them among 27 rides at Dubai Parks and Resorts, 25 minutes from Dubai Marina. For young children, LEGOLAND Dubai is built around LEGO play, from Driving School to the LEGO Factory.

The names many people search for, Ferrari World, Warner Bros. World and SeaWorld, are not in Dubai. They are on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi (Warner Bros. World and SeaWorld quote about 40 minutes from Dubai), and their tickets include no transport from Dubai. Below are 5 Dubai options and 5 Abu Dhabi ones, including the only one with hotel pickup from Dubai.

review: If you can only do one theme park in Dubai, this is the safest bet. For €63 you get unlimited access to 22 rides and attractions spread across six zones, and the whole thing is indoors and temperature-controlled. In a city this hot, that matters as much as the ride list: the weather outside does not change your day here.

The zones are a mix of global brands and in-house worlds. Marvel has the 3D Avengers: Battle of Ultron, Cartoon Network runs live shows, and the Lost Valley pairs coasters with animatronic dinosaurs. Teenagers aged 15+ can add the Haunted Hotel, which younger children cannot enter.

Two catches. The new Kids Zone is not in the ticket; it is bought separately at the park, so families with toddlers should budget for it. And extras add up: the Iron Man experience, arcade games, lockers, pushchairs and souvenir photos are all paid, and outside food is not allowed. Against that, children under 105 cm are free and parking costs nothing, which makes this the cheapest family day on the page.

review: This is the best-value ticket on the page if you have a full day. A one-park ticket at Dubai Parks is €73; this pass is €88 for any two of Motiongate, LEGOLAND Dubai, LEGOLAND Water Park and Real Madrid World. That is about €44 per park, or roughly €15 for the second one.

The pairing that works best for most families is LEGOLAND in the morning and Motiongate after lunch, or LEGOLAND plus LEGOLAND Water Park for younger children. The parks sit around Riverland Dubai and are a 5–10 minute walk apart, so you lose very little time switching.

The catch is stamina: both parks are on the same day, and the ticket does not include transport to Dubai Parks and Resorts on Sheikh Zayed Road, about 25 minutes from Dubai Marina. If you only want one park, buy that park's ticket; if you want the water park, avoid Wednesdays. For more water park options, see our Dubai water parks comparison.

review: Motiongate is the Dubai answer for thrill seekers who do not want to drive to Abu Dhabi. The €73 ticket covers 27 rides and attractions, including 5 roller coasters, a drop tower and a water rapids ride, plus 15 shows such as Step Up Dubai, All In! in the 1,000-seat Hollywood Theatre.

On the IMG Worlds vs Motiongate question: IMG is cheaper (€63), fully indoors and stronger on superhero and dinosaur zones; Motiongate has more coasters and the film-studio lands of Columbia Pictures, DreamWorks Animation and Lionsgate. Visit IMG when it is hot, Motiongate when the weather lets you enjoy walking between rides.

Before buying this ticket alone, look at the Multi Parks Pass: for €15 more you can add LEGOLAND or Real Madrid World next door on the same day. Parking is free; hotel transfers and food are not included.

review: LEGOLAND Dubai is the easiest theme park day on this page for parents of young children. The €73 ticket covers 40+ rides, shows and building experiences across 6 lands, with 15,000 LEGO models made from over 60 million bricks.

The best bits are hands-on rather than fast: the Driving School, where children earn a LEGOLAND Driving Licence, crewing a boat at The Sea Port, and the LEGO Factory, where each child gets a brick to keep. The mix of indoor and outdoor attractions gives you somewhere to cool down between rides.

The listing names no big coasters, so families with teenagers should buy the Multi Parks Pass and split the day with Motiongate. Bring passports or ID; food and transport are extra. Staying near the parks? See our best family resorts in Dubai.

review: Warner Bros. World is the Abu Dhabi park that works best for mixed-age families. The €86 ticket covers 29 rides and attractions in six lands, from Gotham City and Metropolis for the superhero fans to Cartoon Junction and Bedrock for small children, and it is entirely indoors.

Compared with IMG Worlds in Dubai, it is the more character-heavy park, with 35+ live characters, 16 places to eat and 22 shops, and it mixes superhero lands with cartoon lands for younger children. The ticket also skips the ticket-office queue.

The real cost is getting there. The park quotes 40 minutes from Dubai, the ticket includes no transport and the free shuttle has been suspended until further notice. If you are only going for the day, compare it with the day trip with hotel pickup, which has a Warner Bros. option.

review: This is the card that solves the Abu Dhabi problem. The Ferrari World ticket alone is €86 and comes with no transport; this day trip is €127, so for about €42 more you get return hotel pickup from Dubai, an English-speaking guide, bottled water and a visit to the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque.

The park is flexible: choose Ferrari World, Warner Bros. World or SeaWorld when you book. Ferrari World's headliner, Formula Rossa at up to 240 km/h, is listed as under maintenance until further notice, and when it runs it needs an on-site reservation, so thrill seekers should check it before choosing the Ferrari option.

The trade-off is time. In 8–10 hours you cover two long drives and the mosque, so you get less park time than a park-only day. For one Yas park on a short Dubai trip, it is the best balance on this page. More Abu Dhabi day trips are in our guide to Abu Dhabi tours from Dubai.

review: Ferrari World is the park for people who rank theme parks by coasters. The €86 ticket covers 44 rides, attractions, simulators and shows, including the 5D mega-coaster Mission Ferrari, a record-breaking ride with an inverted loop and the Roof Walk.

Read the small print before you go. The park warns that some rides open late or close for maintenance, and the Abu Dhabi day trip at #6 notes that Formula Rossa, its 240 km/h coaster, is under maintenance until further notice. Karting, the Scuderia Challenge F1 simulators and the Quick Pass all cost extra, and outside food is not allowed.

Buy this ticket if you are staying on Yas Island or driving yourself. From Dubai without a car, the day trip at #6 is about €42 more and includes the return transfer. Want other ways to get your heart rate up? See our best adrenaline experiences in Dubai.

review: If you are spending two or more nights in Abu Dhabi, this is the cheapest way into the Yas Island parks. The 2-park pass from €108 works out at about €54 per park, against €86 for a single Ferrari World or Warner Bros. World ticket, and you get 6 days from your first visit to use it. 3- and 4-park versions are offered at checkout.

You can mix the theme parks with Yas Waterworld, and moving between them is easy: parking is free and a free shuttle links the parks, the Yas hotels and Yas Mall. For a single day from Dubai, this pass is the wrong tool: two parks plus the drive there and back is a lot. Do one park a day, and arrive at opening. If water parks are part of the plan, compare Yas Waterworld with the Dubai options in our best water parks in Dubai guide.

review: SeaWorld Abu Dhabi is the pick for families who would rather see marine life than ride coasters. The €73 ticket gives unlimited all-day access to eight indoor realms, animal presentations, 20+ live characters and shows and the world's largest multi-species aquarium, plus one big thrill ride.

It is fully indoors and built around animals rather than speed, so it pairs well with Ferrari World or Warner Bros. World on the multi-park pass. The site also houses SeaWorld Research & Rescue, the region's first marine rescue and rehabilitation centre.

Add-on animal encounters are sold separately, need the general admission ticket and require arrival at Explorer HQ 15 minutes early; minimum age is 2. Parking and the Yas Island shuttle are free, but there is no transport from Dubai in this ticket.

review: Real Madrid World is a niche pick, and a good one if your family wears white on match days. The €73 ticket covers 16 attractions, from the Hala Madrid Coaster and The Wave-La Ola family coaster to the Hands Up! mini drop tower and a lap of the Cibeles fountain on the Champions Bus.

What sets it apart is the club content: Champions Avenue walks you through Real Madrid's big moments and its football and basketball legends, and La Fabrica is a training pitch for kids who want to play rather than ride.

As a stand-alone ticket it is the weakest value here, the same price as Motiongate for fewer rides. It makes far more sense as the second park on the Multi Parks Pass: it opens at noon and stays open until 21:00, so do LEGOLAND or Motiongate in the morning and finish here.

guide.h2: Dubai and Abu Dhabi Theme Parks Compared Side by Side
guide.html:
The ten tickets on the axes that decide the day: indoor or outdoor, who it suits, how intense it is, the from-price, which emirate it is in and whether transport is included. Prices are adult from-prices in euros for a normal date.

Three numbers matter most. IMG Worlds at €63 is the cheapest full-day park and the only Dubai park billed as fully indoor. On a multi pass the second Dubai Parks park costs about €15. And for Abu Dhabi, the day trip at €127 is only about €42 more than a €86 Ferrari World ticket, yet it includes the return drive from your Dubai hotel.

• One park, any season, best value: IMG Worlds of Adventure. Indoors, €63, children under 105 cm free.
  • IMG Worlds vs Motiongate: IMG if it is hot or your group is mixed ages; Motiongate if you want 5 coasters and are visiting in the cooler months.
  • Families with young children: LEGOLAND Dubai, or LEGOLAND plus LEGOLAND Water Park on the Multi Parks Pass (not on a Wednesday).
  • Mixed-age family, one long day: the Multi Parks Pass with LEGOLAND in the morning and Motiongate or Real Madrid World after lunch.
  • Staying in Dubai, want one Abu Dhabi park: the Ferrari World + Mosque day trip, which can also be booked with Warner Bros. World or SeaWorld.
  • Staying 2+ nights on Yas Island: the Yas Island Multi-Park Pass; add Warner Bros. World for small kids, Ferrari World for coasters, SeaWorld for animals.

guide.h2: Practical Tips: Heat, Multi-Park Passes and Getting There
guide.html:
Heat: when to pick an indoor park

Three parks here are sold as indoor: IMG Worlds in Dubai (indoor and temperature-controlled), and Warner Bros. World and SeaWorld on Yas Island. LEGOLAND Dubai mixes indoor and outdoor attractions. The Motiongate, Real Madrid World and Ferrari World tickets do not say, so on a hot day plan around the indoor parks, or use Real Madrid World's late hours: it is open from 12:00 to 21:00.

Combining parks with multi-park passes

At Dubai Parks and Resorts, the Multi Parks Pass gives two parks on the same day for €88, and the gates are a 5–10 minute walk apart. On Yas Island, the Multi-Park Pass gives 2, 3 or 4 parks over 6 days, which is the better fit for a stay in Abu Dhabi.

What costs extra

No ticket on this page includes food, and IMG Worlds and Ferrari World do not allow outside food or drinks. Quick Pass upgrades are sold separately at the Yas Island parks. Watch for park-specific extras: the Kids Zone at IMG Worlds, karting and F1 simulators at Ferrari World and the animal encounters at SeaWorld.

Getting there

Dubai Parks and Resorts (Motiongate, LEGOLAND, Real Madrid World) is on Sheikh Zayed Road, about 25 minutes from Dubai Marina; Motiongate's ticket includes free parking, and none of these tickets includes transport. IMG Worlds has free parking but no pickup. The Yas Island parks are in Abu Dhabi (Warner Bros. World and SeaWorld quote 40 minutes from Dubai); the single-park tickets include no transport and the free shuttle is suspended until further notice, so you need a car, a taxi or the day trip with hotel pickup.

faqs.q: What is the best theme park in Dubai?
faqs.a: IMG Worlds of Adventure for most visitors: it is fully indoor and air-conditioned, has 22 rides across Marvel, Cartoon Network and dinosaur zones, costs from €63 and lets children under 105 cm in free. For coasters pick Motiongate; for young children pick LEGOLAND Dubai.

faqs.q: IMG Worlds vs Motiongate: which is better?
faqs.a: IMG Worlds is cheaper (€63 vs €73), fully indoors and better in the hot months. Motiongate has more rides (27, including 5 roller coasters) and 15 live shows, and you can add a second Dubai Parks park for about €15 with the Multi Parks Pass.

faqs.q: How much are theme park tickets in Dubai?
faqs.a: From €63 for IMG Worlds and €73 each for Motiongate, LEGOLAND Dubai and Real Madrid World. Two Dubai Parks parks on one day cost €88. In Abu Dhabi, Ferrari World and Warner Bros. World start at €86, SeaWorld at €73 and the Yas 2-park pass at €108.

faqs.q: Are Ferrari World and Warner Bros. World in Dubai?
faqs.a: No. Both are on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, with SeaWorld; Warner Bros. World and SeaWorld quote about 40 minutes from Dubai. Their single tickets include no transport. From Dubai, the day trip with hotel pickup (€127) includes the return drive, the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque and entry to Ferrari World, Warner Bros. World or SeaWorld.

faqs.q: Which Dubai theme parks are indoor?
faqs.a: IMG Worlds of Adventure is the fully indoor, temperature-controlled park in Dubai. LEGOLAND Dubai mixes indoor and outdoor attractions. In Abu Dhabi, Warner Bros. World and SeaWorld are indoor parks.

faqs.q: Is a multi-park pass worth it?
faqs.a: Yes if you will really visit two parks. At Dubai Parks and Resorts, two parks on the same day cost €88 instead of €73 for one. On Yas Island, the 2-park pass from €108 works out at about €54 per park and is valid for 6 days, so it suits a stay in Abu Dhabi more than a day trip. For water parks on the same passes, see our Dubai water parks comparison.

faqs.q: Can I cancel Dubai theme park tickets?
faqs.a: All ten tickets on this page offer free cancellation up to 24 hours before, and all five Dubai tickets and the Abu Dhabi day trip also let you reserve now and pay later.

methodology: We compared 10 bookable theme park tickets: five in Dubai (IMG Worlds and the Dubai Parks and Resorts parks, including the multi-park pass) and five in Abu Dhabi, including a day trip with hotel pickup from Dubai. Each was scored on adult price and price per park, indoor or outdoor, ride count and thrill level, who it suits, travel time from Dubai and what you pay for on top (food, fast passes, park extras, transport). Prices are live listing from-prices for a normal date; ratings come from verified guest reviews.
